question.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨5,3,-7⟩+t⟨4,-3,2⟩,\,Π:5x+2y-7z-15=0.
$$
question.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨5+4t,3-3t,-7+2t⟩.
$$

Let's also write the equation of the plane in the dot product form:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+2y-7z-15 & =0 \\ 5x+2y-7z & =15 \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨5,2,-7⟩ & =15 \\ r\cdot ⟨5,2,-7⟩ & =15\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨5+4t,3-3t,-7+2t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨5,2,-7⟩ & =15 \\ ⟨5+4t,3-3t,-7+2t⟩\cdot ⟨5,2,-7⟩ & =15 \\ 5(5+4t)+2(3-3t)-7(-7+2t) & =15 \\ 25+20t+6-6t+49-14t & =15 \\ 80 & =15.\end{aligned}
$$

The equation has no solution. Therefore, we conclude that the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ do not intersect.
